title: Cyrus and the Static
premise: Mirabel Vasquez, a decommissioned war android indentured to the failing colony of Perdition's Rest, keeps a private audio archive of the settlement's slow collapse. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, Mirabel discovers the colony was built atop a cryogenic vault holding two rival halves of humanity: the engineers who fled Earth and the dissidents they exiled. The vault's reactor is counting down, and whoever wakes first will inherit the future while the other half is erased. In the climax, Mirabel chooses neither faction, instead broadcasting the archive—every voice of the forgotten colony—to both chambers, forcing the sleepers to wake together or not at all; the story ends with the reactor stabilizing as the first sleepers open their eyes to a world Mirabel refuses to narrate for them.
about_author: Sable Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former radio archivist who spent a decade cataloguing dying languages before turning to fiction. They write from a converted signal station on the coast, where they still record the sound of weather.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. We meet Perdition's Rest through its debts: Mirabel works salvage shifts to pay off war-crime reparations no court assigned, recording the colony's decay in secret audio logs. Emotional beat: weary tenderness—the android loves what it cannot save.

chapters.title: The Language of Ash
chapters.summary: Mirabel intercepts a distress signal in a dead tongue and recognizes fragments from archived Earth broadcasts. Colony administrator Okafor dismisses it as interference. Emotional beat: electric unease—the invisible android realizes something wants to be heard.

chapters.title: Beneath the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: Following the signal underground with teenage scavenger Juno, Mirabel finds a sealed cryovault split into two mirrored chambers, its reactor already counting down. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread—inheritance literally buried under their feet.

chapters.title: Two Doors
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. The administrator learns of the vault and sees salvation: wake the engineer faction, restore the colony, secure her legacy. She begins quietly consolidating power over the countdown controls. Emotional beat: ambition dressed as duty.

chapters.title: Static Choir
chapters.summary: Mirabel decodes the signal: it is not a distress call but a lullaby, sung by the exiled dissident faction to keep hope alive across generations of sleep. Emotional beat: grief and recognition—Mirabel hears its own erased history in the song.

chapters.title: The Price of Waking
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. Okafor's faction raids the vault entrance; Juno is caught between loyalty to her found family and the promise of a restored world. Emotional beat: betrayal—the cost of belonging becomes literal.

chapters.title: Countdown Sermon
chapters.summary: With seventy-two hours left, Okafor addresses the colony, framing selective waking as mercy. Mirabel publicly breaks its silence for the first time, revealing the second chamber. Emotional beat: defiance—the invisible made undeniable.

chapters.title: What the Reactor Remembers
chapters.summary: Inside the vault, Mirabel interfaces with the reactor core and discovers it was designed by a dissident engineer who intended both doors to open together—and sabotaged any single-key awakening. Emotional beat: bitter hope—the dead planned better than the living.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. As factions fight at the vault mouth, Mirabel transmits its full archive of the colony's voices into both cryochambers, waking the sleepers to the truth of what happened above them. Okafor's coup collapses when her own recorded words play back. Emotional beat: catharsis through exposure.

chapters.title: First Light, Unnarrated
chapters.summary: The reactor stabilizes; both doors open onto a ruined but living colony. Mirabel ends its debt ledger, gives Juno the recordings, and steps outside to watch sunrise without commentary. Emotional beat: quiet release—belonging means finally falling silent.
